approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local graph genetic algorithm whose oracle budget is spent by a Gaussian-process Thompson sampler, with one stagnation reflex added by the previous child. It keeps every scored molecule of the current session in an archive and the best sixty-four as a breeding population, samples breeding parents from high-scoring score quantiles, and builds a fresh field of a hundred and sixty de novo offspring per announced batch of ten, each by connected-fragment crossover with an optional finishing edit or by a short random walk of atom, bond and ring edits. A single shared gate decides what may enter that field: the product must be one ordinary connected graph with legal valences, must survive a parse-and-serialize identity check, must not already be known to this session or to the field being built, and must not introduce a sulfur environment outside a fixed neutral envelope more often than its own scored parents did. Nothing else about the shape or the size of the product is examined. The sampler then fits a Gaussian process to this session's accepted scores using integer-count Morgan fingerprints with a generalized Tanimoto kernel, draws one correlated posterior sample per batch position over the whole field, and sends the sequential sampled maxima to the oracle, each winner removed before the next position. Because the draw is correlated and rewards large sampled residuals, a member the model cannot place at all can still win a position. The only state-dependent part is the inherited stall rule: after three consecutive announced batches that did not raise the session's best score, only the forty highest posterior means stay eligible until the first improving batch.
approach.novelty: This node tests the gate itself rather than the generator, the model or the allocation rule, which is the one stage of this lineage no experiment has ever touched. It adds two objective-blind structural refusals to the single shared admission predicate, applied identically to every origin and every batch: a declared lower bound on heavy-atom count, so products too small to carry any pharmacophore never enter the field, and a refusal of a newly drawn bond that joins two atoms of the same aromatic ring system and closes a three- or four-membered ring through the interior of that aromatic system. Neither rule may read a score, a task identity or any model quantity; both are pure functions of the proposed graph. The two together are one intervention on one predicate, chosen because the Parent's own receipts show them removing the two channels that no objective rewards on purpose. Siblings on this Parent changed the predictor, the retention rule, the stall-episode length and the stall exit condition, and the campaign's two earlier coarse-chemistry attempts replaced the operator repertoire on a different Parent; none of them altered what a generated molecule must look like to be eligible at all. The honest shape of the test is registered in advance: because this benchmark does not price chemical viability and one of the two channels carries part of this Anchor's own realized gain, a loss is a real answer about the scoring surface rather than an implementation fault.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent Anchor n-61b9b3bfb40d scores macro 0.607030 (SD 0.030175; seed macros 0.649701 / 0.585234 / 0.586156) and gained +0.010577 paired over n-1744a1494180 by restricting stalled candidate eligibility; its ten-hunk diff and receipts were re-read. Its shared pool-admission predicate still tests only connectivity, valence, a stable canonical identity, novelty and the narrow source-relative sulfur gate, so two degenerate output channels that h-0df1b8bbf732f363 counted on the Anchor's own byte-identical reproduction n-cf8d309c06de reach the allocator unchecked. A read-only replay over the Parent's own 15 published sessions (435 pools, 69,600 pool members, 76,054 valid generated candidates, 4,350 proposals) reproduces that finding's 98 fragment proposals and the recomputed whole-run increment mass 5.978073 over 253 improvements exactly, and adds the pool-level picture. Channel one, size: 2,286 of 69,600 pool members (3.28 per cent) carry six or fewer heavy atoms. Their integer-count fingerprints are nearly empty, so kernel similarity to every scored record is near zero and they occupy the top of the uncertainty ordering: mean posterior-SD rank 3.0 of 160, 2,285 of 2,286 inside the top sixteen, and the single most uncertain member of the field is one of them in 421 of 435 batches, which lifts the field's maximum posterior SD to 0.982 of the fitted score scale at the median against 0.878 for its largest member above the floor. The allocator therefore buys them at the exploration end: 98 of the 997 mask-free picks ranked 40 or worse by posterior mean are such members (their own mean-rank median 135, SD-rank median 1), every one of the 98 scored below its session median, none entered any top decile, none improved an incumbent, and they arrive as late as evaluation 298 of 300, whereas the other 899 tail picks put 221 above the median and bought 32 incumbent improvements. The smallest molecule in any session's top decile holds 23 heavy atoms. Channel two, transannular aromatic closure: 1,974 pool members (2.84 per cent) and 140 proposals contain a non-aromatic bond joining two atoms of one aromatic cycle and closing a ring of three or four atoms through its interior. This channel is concentrated rather than diffuse: 1,596 of those pool members and 133 of those proposals sit in two of fifteen sessions, where it supplied 33 top-decile proposals and 11 of the 253 incumbent improvements. So the admission path both spends budget on a measurably worthless channel and carries part of this Anchor's realized gain on a second one, and nothing in the campaign has yet measured what the same 300 calls buy once both are refused.

literature_review.conclusion: The searches answered one question and left the mechanism resting on internal evidence. The question they answered: a lower bound on product size at the admission point is this method family's own original design, present in both the Jensen graph GA and the GuacaMol baseline port as more than five atoms, and removed on purpose in the Mol GA reference this lineage is rooted in, whose documentation redirects size control into the objective function. On this benchmark that redirection has no addressee, because the objectives do not price size and the contract forbids reading them, so the floor is restored at the only remaining place, the shared admission predicate. The searches also supplied a direct caution. The same reference code screens rings with ring_OK, and replaying ring_OK over the Anchor's own 4,350 proposals refuses 1,364 of them, 166 of 443 top-decile proposals and the final best molecule of five of the fifteen sessions, so adopting it would be a large uncontrolled intervention on this Anchor's scoring surface; this position therefore takes none of its three rules and refuses only the single transannular closure the Anchor's own counts name. What the literature does not supply is any parameter: the floor of seven heavy atoms is set from this Anchor's own replayed counts, where every one of 98 sub-floor proposals scored below its session median and the smallest molecule in any session's top decile holds 23 heavy atoms, and the closure size of four is the size the Anchor's own output actually produces. Literature origin is not permission to continue: one complete exposed panel ends this configuration, and if both rules fire at their forecast rates while realized increments and the panel do not rise, the channel hypothesis is recorded as refuted for this Anchor with no floor sweep and no second configuration.

hypothesis: Two objective-blind structural predicates are added to the shared generated-pool admission path of the Anchor, applied to every candidate from every origin in every batch, after the inherited checked-graph and identity admission and before the novelty and sulfur checks that stay exactly as inherited. Rule one, the size floor: a candidate whose heavy-atom count is below seven is refused, so no molecule of six or fewer heavy atoms can enter a fresh field, be priced by the posterior, or receive an oracle call. Rule two, the transannular aromatic closure refusal: a candidate is refused when it contains a non-aromatic bond whose two atoms both lie in one connected system of aromatic bonds, are joined by that aromatic system, and are separated in it by a shortest aromatic path of two or three bonds, that is when the new bond closes a three- or four-membered ring through the interior of an aromatic ring or fused aromatic system. Both are pure functions of the proposed molecular graph: no accepted score, no score level, no task identity, no model quantity and no corpus lookup enters either decision. Refused candidates consume a generation attempt exactly as an inherited rejection does and are absorbed by the inherited bounded retry path, so the field target, the batch size, the posterior fit, the correlated draw and its consumption, the stall counter, the stall mask and the fallback routing are untouched; the mechanism's only effect is on the composition of the field the allocator is allowed to price.

finding_summary.headline: Both rules fired and both waste channels are gone, yet increments fell 0.648 and the panel 0.0432: the registered scientific falsifier triggered
finding_summary.insights:
The admission half of the open admission-versus-operator question now has a measured answer on this Anchor, and it is negative: the two degenerate output channels the chemistry audits kept naming can be removed completely, at full enforcement and negligible cost, and the search does not get better. Removing measurable waste is not the same as creating gain. The fragment channel was real waste by every intermediate measure - 2,286 of 69,600 admitted members, the single most uncertain member of the field in 421 of 435 batches, 98 oracle calls every one of which scored below its session median and improved nothing - and refusing it bought the same 32 tail improvements and a lower realized increment mass. The honest conclusion is the one the intent registered in advance: on this scoring surface the budget spent on the degenerate channels was not the binding constraint, so no floor sweep, no closure-size variant and no valence-context extension follows from this node, and the named successor needs its own forecast and its own test rather than this node's authority.

Two things the campaign believed about this experiment turned out to be path properties rather than rule properties. First, the closure channel's concentration does not transfer: in the Anchor's stream two of fifteen sessions carried 1,596 of 1,974 closure pool members, but in this node's own stream those sessions refuse 0.46 and 0.16 per cent of examined candidates while the heaviest closure load moves to seed-0 deco_hop and the zaleplon cells. A session partition defined on the Parent's realization cannot be used to separate two rules in a Child that diverges from the Parent at its first refusal - here batch one, attempt seventy, on a two-atom candidate. Any future attempt to separate the floor from the closure rule has to do it by running them separately, not by splitting sessions. Second, this round's law-free reference is now the right lens for the whole panel: it already showed that both of the Anchor's high seed-0 cells belong to its particular path, and this node loses them in almost exactly the same way. Reading the two together, the campaign should stop treating deco_hop seed 0 as evidence about any intervention on this Anchor.

What the evidence does add about the method is a size asymmetry. The floor is a lower bound with no upper counterpart, and the operator repertoire has no contraction move of comparable strength to its growth moves: nothing in any trajectory trims an overgrown molecule back to a ring system. With the only downward pressure at admission now one-sided, the admitted field shifted up by about 6 heavy atoms and this node bought 428 molecules above 50 heavy atoms against the Anchor's 44, including 181 and 207 in two deco_hop cells whose scores never left the 0.605-0.614 plateau, and 102 candidates rejected by the inherited 120-atom cap. That runaway is not new and is not this node's invention - the law-free re-draw, which changed no rule, produced 288 such picks in a deco_hop cell of its own - but the mirror image is what cost the one unexplained cell: in drd2 seed 1 the Anchor's win came from contracting 38 heavy atoms down to 23, and a field whose compact region had shrunk to a tenth of its former share never found it. The method class that would address this is not a different floor value but a size-symmetric proposal or admission scheme: a contraction or whole-ring-system replacement operator weighted comparably to the growth moves, or an admission window defined relative to the breeding parents a product came from rather than an absolute bound.

Two further diagnoses from this node's own trajectories bear on where the remaining headroom is. Late budget buys almost nothing: the median session took only 15.2 per cent of its total gain after evaluation 150 (the Anchor 18.1 per cent), and the molecular report shows the tail spent on score-identical isosteres, two molecules sharing 0.46092619586 and differing only by N-F against N-Br, with scaffolds inherited from the starting pool and decorated rather than replaced. And the surrogate's ranking is fine while its uncertainty scale is wrong in a task-dependent way that this intervention did not touch: improvers sit at a median posterior-mean rank of 6 of 160 on both sides, yet only 17.4 per cent of sitagliptin picks land within one posterior standard deviation of their predicted mean and 40.3 per cent land more than three below it, against 94.5 per cent within one standard deviation on median_2 - essentially identical in the Anchor (19.2, 42.3, 95.6). Because the error runs in opposite directions across tasks, no single noise or amplitude constant fixes it; an online-calibrated or heavy-tailed heteroscedastic surrogate would be the class of change that could. Taken with this result, the evidence now points away from the product-admission predicate and toward the proposal repertoire and the surrogate's uncertainty as the places where this lineage is actually bound - a reading that should be finished against the operator-granularity position running in parallel on this same Parent and profile.
finding_summary.results:
Both rules executed on every generated candidate in all fifteen sessions and the two target channels are gone. Of 78,031 valid candidates examined, 3,144 were refused (4.03 per cent, inside the forecast two-to-five band): 2,767 by the heavy-atom floor (3.55 per cent, per-session 1.76-5.56 per cent, non-zero in 430 of 435 batches) and 377 by the transannular closure refusal (0.48 per cent, ring size four in 369 cases and three in eight). Both rules fired in 15 of 15 sessions, so neither is dormant. No admitted pool member of the 69,600 and no accepted molecule of the 4,350 violates either rule, confirmed by re-deriving both predicates from the molecules themselves; the Anchor's own stream carries 2,286 sub-floor pool members, 1,974 closure members, 98 sub-floor picks and 140 closure picks.

The field's composition changed as predicted at the bottom and not as predicted above it. The 0-6 heavy-atom band emptied (2,286 to 0), but its mass did not reappear just above the floor: the 7-15 bands are essentially unchanged (2,032 to 1,987) while the 26-30 band collapsed from 23,351 to 13,479 and the 36-plus band doubled from 11,401 to 24,540, lifting the mean admitted size from 29.4 to 34.8 heavy atoms. This is the wholesale upward shift the observable was written to be able to show, and it starts immediately: at batch one, with identical populations, the admitted field is already 1.0 heavy atoms larger, growing to about 6 by batch ten. Every batch still filled to exactly 160 with no truncation. The uncertainty reading moved exactly as forecast: the median of the field's maximum posterior standard deviation over the fitted score scale, over all 435 announced batches, fell from 0.9823 to 0.8909 (quartiles 0.8297 and 0.9417 against 0.9576 and 0.9987), and the number of batches whose single most uncertain member is a sub-floor fragment fell from 421 of 435 to zero; the most uncertain member is now a 10-heavy-atom molecule at the median instead of a 2-atom one. The extra rejections were absorbed: breeding attempts rose from 76,057 to 78,155 (mean 174.8 to 179.7 per batch, maximum 199 to 203 against the limit of 50,000) with zero truncated batches, zero exhaustion errors and zero posterior fallbacks.

The budget freed from the two channels bought nothing. The 98 fragment picks and 140 closure picks fell to zero. The exploration-end picks they had occupied were re-spent above the floor and did slightly better in a weak sense - 246 of 900 mask-free picks ranked fortieth or worse landed above their session median, against 221 of 997 for the Anchor - but they bought exactly the same 32 incumbent improvements. Whole-run realized increment mass fell from 5.978073 over 253 improvements to 5.330399 over 289 improvements, down 0.647674 and lower in 11 of 15 sessions. Both registered session groups fell: the thirteen closure-dormant sessions went 5.264193 to 4.689375 (-0.574817) and the two closure-heavy sessions, seed-2 deco_hop and seed-2 sitagliptin_mpo, went 0.713880 to 0.641024 (-0.072857). The registered "rules need separation" branch, which requires a rise confined to the thirteen while the two fall, therefore does not apply; the main scientific falsifier does, because the rules fired at forecast rates and the fragment band emptied while increments and the panel both failed to rise.

The panel fell on every seed: paired delta -0.043178 over matched seeds 0/1/2 (-0.063587, -0.043393, -0.022554), macro mean 0.563852 against 0.607030, four of fifteen cells up and eleven down, against a registered minimum effect of +0.002. Read against this round's law-free reference on this same Anchor, whose own luck band is -0.055482 to +0.014579 at a realized -0.020452, the delta lies inside the band, so its magnitude is not separable from path luck. The cell-by-cell reading is sharper than the mean. The largest single loss, deco_hop seed 0 at 0.856148 to 0.610130, is reproduced by that pure re-draw, which lost the same cell to 0.607697; this node is in fact 0.002433 above it there. The second fragile high cell, sitagliptin_mpo seed 0, went 0.765861 to 0.650421 against the re-draw's 0.670248. Exactly one cell is not explained by path luck: drd2_docking seed 1, where the Anchor reached 0.999992 and the re-draw 0.991320 but this node stopped at 0.795923, which alone is about -0.013 of the macro mean. In that cell the Anchor's decisive move was a size contraction to a 23-heavy-atom compact molecule at evaluation 34, and this node's field barely contained that region - 9.7 per cent of pooled members at or below 25 heavy atoms against 39.9 per cent, five accepted picks against 111 - while the session's own 115 refusals were all 1-5 atom fragments plus six large closures, so no refusal removed a molecule near the Anchor's winning chain. Increment mass tells the same mixed story: the single available law-free realization on this Anchor sits at 5.671299, so roughly half of the 0.648 drop is reproduced by changing nothing but the path, and this node is a further 0.341 below that one realization.

That runaway is not new and is not this node's invention - the law-free re-draw, which changed no rule, produced 288 such picks in a deco_hop cell of its own - but the mirror image is what cost the one unexplained cell: in drd2 seed 1 the Anchor's win came from contracting 38 heavy atoms down to 23, and a field whose compact region had shrunk to a tenth of its former share never found it. The method class that would address this is not a different floor value but a size-symmetric proposal or admission scheme: a contraction or whole-ring-system replacement operator weighted comparably to the growth moves, or an admission window defined relative to the breeding parents a product came from rather than an absolute bound.

Two further diagnoses from this node's own trajectories bear on where the remaining headroom is. Late budget buys almost nothing: the median session took only 15.2 per cent of its total gain after evaluation 150 (the Anchor 18.1 per cent), and the molecular report shows the tail spent on score-identical isosteres, two molecules sharing 0.46092619586 and differing only by N-F against N-Br, with scaffolds inherited from the starting pool and decorated rather than replaced. And the surrogate's ranking is fine while its uncertainty scale is wrong in a task-dependent way that this intervention did not touch: improvers sit at a median posterior-mean rank of 6 of 160 on both sides, yet only 17.4 per cent of sitagliptin picks land within one posterior standard deviation of their predicted mean and 40.3 per cent land more than three below it, against 94.5 per cent within one standard deviation on median_2 - essentially identical in the Anchor (19.2, 42.3, 95.6). Because the error runs in opposite directions across tasks, no single noise or amplitude constant fixes it; an online-calibrated or heavy-tailed heteroscedastic surrogate would be the class of change that could. Taken with this result, the evidence now points away from the product-admission predicate and toward the proposal repertoire and the surrogate's uncertainty as the places where this lineage is actually bound - a reading that should be finished against the operator-granularity position running in parallel on this same Parent and profile.

molecular.headline: Mid-size halogen-decorated fused heteroaromatics; the heavy-atom floor and transannular refusal both hold in what was bought.
molecular.overall_character: Across 4350 optimizer-proposed molecules (290 per task-seed, 870 per objective in the digest) the generator emits ring-dense, strongly aromatic, uncharged, flat chemistry. Digest string counters read ring_closure_rate 0.9954-1.0 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.992-1.0 on every objective, charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 everywhere, and halogen_rate 0.22-0.998. Mean size per objective runs 24.7 to 49.0 heavy atoms by my reading of the trajectories, with mean SMILES length 43.7 to 85.9 in the digest. The two new structural rules are visible in the output: no proposed molecule anywhere has fewer than seven heavy atoms (minimum exactly 7) and none closes a three- or four-membered ring through an aromatic system, where the paired Parent trajectories contain 98 sub-seven-atom molecules (minimum 1 heavy atom) and 140 such small transannular closures. What remains is chemistry whose liabilities are bonded rather than sized: N-F and N-Br amides (946 of 4350), alkyl peroxides and peroxy esters (234), N-O single bonds (434), aminals (466), free thiols (551) and fluoromethyl groups (654), while trifluoromethyl appears in exactly zero molecules of either this node or its Parent.

Digest counters: ring_closure_rate 1.0, aromatic_atom_rate 1.0, halogen_rate 0.9368, charged_rate 0.0, stereocentre_rate 0.0. Seed 0 and seed 1 converge on an N-halogenated anilide; seed 2 keeps the indole-2-carboxamide of the initial pool and swaps its methoxys for methyls.

The low end is a single methylated fluorobenzene, Cc1ccc(F)cc1 at 0.0, which is the floor-admitted but essentially featureless end of the pool.

The worst end is the floor-admitted minimum, an acyclic polyene C=NC=CC=CC and a carbonate CCOOC(=O)OC at 0.5-0.5004, which still clear the seven heavy atom rule.

Seeds 0 and 2 end on compact two-aromatic-system molecules: seed 0 on an N-aryl azetidine/pyrrolidine joined to a 3-amino-5-fluorophenyl dihydropyridine (top 30 mean 31.2 heavy atoms, 2.0 aromatic rings), seed 2 on a pyrrolidine whose nitrogen carries a CH2-sulfinyl-(3-chlorophenyl) arm next to a fused dihydrobenzofuran (31.7 heavy atoms, 2.0 aromatic rings). Seed 1 is a different compound class: larger (top 30 mean 34.3 heavy atoms), three aromatic rings, built on a dibenzofuran-type bridged biaryl ether (aryl-O-aryl plus a direct biaryl bond in 29 of its top 30) attached through an alpha-chloro aminal CH(Cl)N and an exocyclic enamine to a 2-aryl imidazolidine/hexahydropyrimidine aminal. Its longest path between aromatic systems averages about 10 bonds against 7.6-7.8 bonds in the other two seeds, so the pharmacophore is stretched out rather than compact. Seed 1 also keeps the initial pool's 3,5-dichlorophenyl sulfonamide far longer: 226 of its 290 proposals contain an S(=O)N group, last seen at evaluation 259, against 27 of 290 (last at evaluation 40) in seed 0 and 65 of 290 (last at evaluation 90) in seed 2.

In seed 1 the same gradient is followed with sulfonamide still attached (0.4484 at evaluation 102) and only reaches 0.7959 at evaluation 281, where the nitrogen is an aryl-substituted aminal inside a dibenzofuran-bearing framework rather than an alkylated amine on a small two-ring core.

The dominant core is the purinedione / imidazopyrimidinedione of the initial pool with fluorine placed on ring nitrogen, n-F or N-F appearing in 525 of this objective's 870 proposals and fluoromethyl in 359; seed 1's best molecules strip the second ring down to an acyclic imine chain with a fluorocyclopentene, seed 2 keeps a three-aromatic-ring aniline-substituted dione with a thiol-terminated ethyl arm.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient tracks fluorine count on a 25-27 heavy atom heteroaromatic dione: 0.6878 and 0.6504 molecules carry four to five fluorines, while the 0.0 end of the pool is unfluorinated or singly fluorinated fragments such as FC1C=CC(C2=CCC=C2)=C1 and the initial diphenyl dione at 0.0021. Crucially the fluorine is bought as N-F, n-F and CH2F rather than as aryl-F or CF3, and a single ring-nitrogen change from n2cc3 to n2nc3 drops a final molecule from 0.4739 to 0.0797, so the gradient is sharply sensitive to the heteroatom pattern the generator perturbs freely.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Over the 4350 proposals I read, 1026 carry a halogen bonded to nitrogen (946 of them N-F, 551 of those on an aromatic ring nitrogen), 654 carry a fluoromethyl group, 82 carry an O-halogen bond and exactly 0 carry a trifluoromethyl group; the trifluoromethyl count is also 0 across the 4350 paired baseline proposals. On two objectives the N-halogen appears in all thirty of the top-scoring molecules, so this is not a tail artefact but the motif the search optimises.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator places halogens on nitrogen and oxygen as freely as on carbon, and never builds a trifluoromethyl group.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A halogenation or atom-replacement operator that is valence-legal but chemistry-blind. It would have to restrict halogen attachment to carbon environments and offer the common polyfluorinated carbon groups as single composite edits, so that a request for more fluorine is answered on carbon instead of on a heteroatom.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest charged_rate is 0.0 on all five objectives, 4350 of 4350 proposals neutral, even in the pools where saturated basic amines occur in up to nine tenths of molecules and where the initial pool supplied a carboxylic acid.
transferable_gaps.gap: No proposal carries a formal charge, so ionization state is outside the generator's reach.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation and operators never alter protonation or produce a counter-ion-free ionic form. A generator able to propose the charged tautomer of an amine or an acid, or to pair an acid with a basic centre inside one molecule, would cover a region of chemistry currently unreachable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on every objective while my reading of the same molecules finds an undefined sp3 stereocentre in 2324 of the 4350 proposals; the molecules grow benzylic and ring carbons with four different substituents and leave every one unassigned.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemistry is created but never specified.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Edits act on a flat graph with no configuration channel. Adding stereo assignment as an edit, and keeping assignments through crossover, would let the generator distinguish molecules that it currently proposes as one undifferentiated string.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 428 of 4350 proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms against 44 of 4350 in the paired baseline, and on one objective the top-scoring molecules reach 70-81 heavy atoms and a 214-character SMILES made of repeating aryl-ether and amidine units, scoring within 0.005 of a 31-heavy-atom fused heteroaromatic in another seed of the same pool. No trajectory contains a step that shortens such an oligomer.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular size moves in one direction only; nothing trims an overgrown molecule back to a ring system.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The new lower heavy-atom floor has no upper counterpart and the operator mix has no contraction move of comparable strength to its growth moves. A size-symmetric operator set, or an admission rule bounding growth relative to the pool it breeds from, would stop budget being spent on homologue series.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 234 of 4350 proposals contain an O-O bond, concentrated at 194 on a single objective where they appear in top-scoring molecules as peroxy esters; 434 contain an N-O single bond, 292 of them on one objective where the best molecule carries the N-O ring; and 466 contain an aminal, including every molecule in one cell's top thirty. The paired baseline carries the same motifs at roughly half these rates (118, 251, 445).
transferable_gaps.gap: Peroxide, N-O, N-N and aminal bonds are treated as ordinary edits and reach the top-scoring sets.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The structural admission rules now added cover size and one ring-closure pathology but not bond-level implausibility. A graph-only, objective-blind refusal of heteroatom-heteroatom peroxide and N-O linkages, or an operator that never forms them, would keep these out of the pool the surrogate then learns from.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The best molecule of several cells is a substituent-level edit of the highest-scoring member of the shared starting pool: an indole-2-carboxamide starting molecule reappears as the best molecule of one cell, a phenyl purinedione starting molecule supplies the core of the best molecules on two different objectives, and in one cell the dichlorophenyl sulfonamide starting molecule persists in 226 of 290 proposals, its saturated diamine ring surviving into that cell's best molecule after the sulfonyl group is finally dropped at proposal 281. Different seeds of one objective end on chemically unrelated cores, each the core its own starting pool offered.
transferable_gaps.gap: Scaffolds are inherited from the starting pool and decorated, not replaced.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator set edits atoms and bonds inside a given framework but has no move that exchanges a whole ring system, and no mechanism carries a motif found productive in one pool into another. A ring-system replacement operator, or a motif store shared across independent pools, would make the search's reachable set larger than its starting set.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The highest-scoring molecules in several cells form families differing in one halogen: two molecules in one pool share the score 0.46092619586 differing only by N-F against N-Br, and four share 0.44989726212 across F, Cl and Br permutations at two positions. The final six proposals of several cells are such permutations.
transferable_gaps.gap: At convergence the generator can only permute substituent identity, producing score-identical isosteres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: When the local neighbourhood is flat the generator has no larger-radius structural move to fall back on, so the tail of the budget buys chemically equivalent molecules. A move that changes ring topology or linker length once substituent edits stop changing the objective value would convert that tail into information.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
